text:
Alex: Quick sync — weekly GPU capacity review. TL;DR: us-west and eu-central look tight over the next 72h. ap-southeast had a networking egress spike yesterday but is currently fine. Uploaded the live sheet: https://redwood.internal/sheets/gpu-forecast. Main asks: decisions on burst/provisioning, node pre-warm, and any cost tradeoffs.

Riley: On it. Per-cluster burn rates in the sheet — us-west-2 projected to hit ~92% GPU-hour utilization by Thu 18:00 UTC if current queue stays. Latency SLOs start degrading around 95%.

Sam: Can we move non-urgent batch to eu-west-1? I see ~20% spare capacity there for the next 48h.

Maria: Heads-up — eu-central-1 has a planned firmware window this Fri 02:00–06:00 UTC. Ops will take 3 racks (12 nodes) offline, ~80 GPU-hours lost. I can postpone if we need the capacity.

Joel: I've submitted a spot replacement/burst request to our provider — ETA 18–24h. Also recommend enabling quantized variants for the recommender (q4f16) for a canary run; should cut per-token GPU time ~25–35% on that workload.

capacity-bot: ALERT: cluster redwood-w-usw2 high burn rate (90%). Auto-scale disabled for reserved-cap accounts.

Alex: Options on the table: 1) provider burst (fast, expensive) 2) shift low-priority batch to eu-west (cheap, moves load) 3) canary quantized models for inference (low-risk, needs smoke tests). What's the preferred sequence?

Riley: My vote: start canary for recommender + move batch jobs first. Simultaneously request 4 A100 instances in us-west as short-term buffer (prebuy for 48h). If canary shows perf regression, we'll fall back and keep nodes. Approve?

Sam: :thumbsup: Approved from platform ops. I'll open job reroutes and adjust priorities — target start in 2 hours.

Maria: I can delay the firmware to Sat 02:00 UTC to avoid the Friday hit. Will file a change and notify security. Ops prefers Saturday maintenance.

Joel: Fine to delay. Cost estimate for provider burst: ~+$8k/day for the requested capacity. Canary quantization rollout testing overhead ~2–3 engineer hours.

Alex: Good. Maria, please post the change link here. Riley/Sam coordinate the reroute + canary. I'll watch the dashboards and ALBs. Also, Sam — please investigate the ap-southeast egress spike and add caching if needed; flagging if >300MB/s on egress.

Sam: Noted. The spike looked like a large dataset pull from analytics yesterday — adding a caching layer on the ingest path should smooth it. I'll open a PR and include a short rollout plan.

Riley: Quick autoscaler snippet for anyone who needs it (we'll apply to the batch runtime):

```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-runtime
spec:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: nvidia.com/gpu
      targetAverageUtilization: 70
```

Alex: Thanks. Also tracking action items: (1) Riley -> request 4 A100s in us-west (prebuy 48h), (2) Sam -> reroute batch + open PR for caching, (3) Maria -> change request for firmware move + confirm, (4) Joel -> monitor cost/spot updates. I'll update the sheet after these actions and close loop by EOD.

Riley: Request submitted to provider (ticket #PR-7885). ETA 18h.

capacity-bot: UPDATE: provider ticket PR-7885 acknowledged. Estimated provisioning 18–20h.

Sam: PR for caching opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/412. Plan includes a 10-minute canary then full switch.

Maria: Change request filed: https://redwood.internal/changerequests/542 — moved firmware to Sat 02:00 UTC. Security signed off.

Joel: Noted. Will keep an eye on cost delta; will post a short breakdown once the provider confirms delivery and billing fine print.

Alex: Great work. I'll monitor dashboards and re-open thread if anything slips. If the canary hits any quality drift, revert immediately. :eyes:

Riley: Quick follow-up in case it helps — if we need longer-term smoothing, consider increasing reserved capacity for us-west by 2 racks in the next commit cycle; cost vs predictability tradeoff in the sheet.

Alex: Copy. We'll table that for the monthly finance review unless we see repeats this month.

(2h update) Riley: Provider confirmed delivery ETA 17.5h. Spun up 2 nodes for interim buffer. Us-west 1h burn rate dropped to 86%.

Alex: Closing for now. Reopen if new alerts fire. :white_check_mark:
